checks: The barycentric inequalities lambda_i and lambda_j at least one third give three cones from the centroid with disjoint interiors, and their intersections with K are the three negative triangles.

In the basis of the two positive ray endpoints, any point outside the cone violating a+b at most one produces a segment from it to a ray endpoint that crosses the other ray strictly beyond the outer endpoint. Convexity rules this out. The old clipped cone then equals the triangle spanned by the centroid and its two endpoints.

All six endpoints survive the other cuts. The clipped old body and the replacement therefore have the same triangle in each negative cone. Removed old area has density minus two and the enlargement contributes only density plus one off those triangles.

For the boundary case, Minkowski interpolation includes a small translated copy of K about the centroid. For a full-dimensional Q every interior point eventually belongs to the interpolates by dilating slightly about the centroid in reverse, and exterior points eventually do not belong. A lower-dimensional Q has area zero, so its exterior already suffices. Dominated convergence passes both areas to the limit.
